input: nums contains n integers in[-1000000000,1000000000], including empty input. Collections are ordinary finite dense arrays/lists, not subclasses, proxies, sparse/accessor-backed collections. Strings are ordinary/primitive strings. Every collection length and computed allocation size fits [0,4294967295], with padded sizes explicitly included. No concurrent mutation or built-in monkey-patching is allowed. Preconditions are not runtime-checked, and allocation/resource capacity or completion is not guaranteed by declared bounds. JavaScript integer inputs are primitive safe-integer Number, excluding negative zero, NaN, infinities, fractions and BigInt.
return: Fresh array containing the same multiset, ordered by increasing occurrence frequency and, among equal frequencies, decreasing numeric value.
mutation_aliasing: Inputs and caller-held aliases remain unchanged; only private working state is used. The Solution instance retains no state. The sort operates only on a new outer array; output never aliases nums.
numeric: Frequency differences are at most n and value comparator differences at most2000000000. Negating bounded input values and all sort keys is exact. Equal values are indistinguishable scalar occurrences. All integer inputs/intermediates remain within [-9007199254740991,9007199254740991]; no bitwise coercion is used.
complexity: Expected O(n log(n+1)+1) time under hash-map/comparison-sort assumptions and O(n+1) auxiliary/output storage including frequency map, copied array, sort keys/workspace. Bounds include ordinary built-in operations/allocations and assume bounded-word arithmetic, constant-time indexing, amortized append/pop and any explicitly stated hash/sort behavior.
source_accounting: The complete standalone source is 379 UTF-8 bytes, including every helper, Solution wrapper, signature, loop, built-in call, annotation/comment, whitespace and terminal newline.
